title: Probabilistic electrical power demand forecasting with uncertainty quantification
note: arXiv abstract page (v1 only, 28 Sep 2026, cs.LG): compares NGBoost, a Bayesian model, MC Dropout and Gaussian process regression on power-consumption data; says NGBoost has the lowest MAE and RMSE in every zone with high interval coverage and fairly narrow intervals. Abstract gives no numbers, dataset, horizon or inputs. No code or data link on the page. Paper text licence CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

title: Probabilistic electrical power demand forecasting with uncertainty quantification (full text)
note: Results table, NGBoost by zone: MAE 1682.57 / 1400.45 / 1265.71; RMSE 2241.14 / 1799.98 / 1760.22; 95% interval coverage 0.95 / 0.96 / 0.96. Next best MAE is MC Dropout: 3014.88 / 2232.26 / 2496.89 (coverage 0.92 / 0.86 / 0.77). Bayesian linear regression MAE 3454.93 / 2659.66 / 3410.88. No MAPE, no intervals on the scores, units not restated in the table.

title: Probabilistic electrical power demand forecasting with uncertainty quantification (full text)
note: Gaps: no hyperparameters for any model; no code or data availability statement; no pre-registration; no pretrained or foundation model. Gaussian process row looks broken: MAE 17950 to 32366, coverage 0.00 and an identical interval width (1239.59) in all three zones. All four models appear to share one feature set but the paper does not say so outright. No naive or seasonal baseline.

title: Search: paper title + authors + NGBoost Tetouan code github (no result)
note: One web search for the paper's code or an independent replication found nothing: no repository by the authors and no third-party rerun. It returned only unrelated projects on the same public Tetouan consumption dataset and the original NGBoost paper; none were opened or used.

title: Probabilistic electrical power demand forecasting with uncertainty quantification (full text)
note: Setup: Tetouan (Morocco) utility SCADA data, three zones, year 2017, 10-minute readings aggregated to hourly. Chronological 80/20 split; test length not stated (about 73 days by my arithmetic). Horizon never given. Inputs: hour, day, month, temperature, humidity, wind speed, two diffuse-flow measures; no lag features; not stated whether weather is known-future.
